subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: Should Windows/QuickStart Anthropic setup change the default away from Opus, add a paid-credit readiness probe or warning before Hatch in Terminal, or do both?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing model defaults and deciding whether onboarding may call a paid live probe affects provider policy, setup cost, and first-run UX.

options.title: Probe or Warn Before Hatch
options.body: Keep provider choice intact, but require onboarding to prove or plainly warn about Anthropic billing readiness before launching the first terminal chat.

options.title: Change the Anthropic Default
options.body: Move QuickStart away from Opus/high-cost Anthropic defaults and cover fresh install plus existing-config behavior in docs and tests.

options.title: Keep Opus With Explicit Confirmation
options.body: Leave the current model policy in place but make the paid-credit requirement explicit before completion so the first chat failure is not surprising.

recommendation.title: Probe or Warn Before Hatch
recommendation.body: Keep provider choice intact, but require onboarding to prove or plainly warn about Anthropic billing readiness before launching the first terminal chat.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent onboarding setup-ladder and macOS first-chat verification work make this the closest current product/code ownership signal.
